vision.outputText: The Garten-Golum poster titled "Formen der Abweichung" features a central figure with an exact face rendered in a green botanical style, resembling a plant-based humanoid. The face is detailed with luminous eyes that glow softly, and the entire figure is textured with a coloured-pencil effect, giving it a hand-drawn, organic feel. Around the head, various plant-like extensions bloom, each labeled with names of artists or performers such as Tuli Mekondjo, Catherine Lorent, Stefan Kaminski, and others, arranged in a balanced layout. The typography of the title "Formen der Abweichung" is bold and yellow, set against a green diamond-patterned background at the top, with smaller text in pink and black providing additional event details. The bottom section of the poster contains venue and event information in a mix of bright pink, green, and yellow text on a dark background, specifying the location (CANK Neukölln, Karl-Marx-Straße 95, 12043 Berlin), dates (6.9.–12.9.2026),

rawScenePlan.title: Formen der Abweichung — Aisle Echo
rawScenePlan.event: A barcode-bearing ISBN sticker folded over the edge of a returned art-catalog stack catches the pulsed fluorescent glint; that striped reflection lines up with the mirrored column duplicating the Garten-Golum poster, and the poster's luminous eyes track the pattern. A thin paper tendril peels free from the poster,
rawScenePlan.transformationMechanism: optical resonance and mechanical leverage — pulsed fluorescent light and reflected barcode pattern
rawScenePlan.monsterPresence: partial — Garten-Golum visible as animated poster face and a single emerging paper tendril; creature
rawScenePlan.consequence: A cracked fluorescent tube hangs askew over the counter, a thin dust veil drifting in the air; the metal price-rail is ajar and a curled ISBN sticker lies hooked under it with its free edge visible and ready to slide.
rawScenePlan.nextHook: curled ISBN sticker folded under the ajar metal price-rail clip; its free curved edge is visible and begins to slide in the following motion.
rawScenePlan.stillPrompt: Interior Kaufhaus aisle at late-1980s scale: dusty concrete floor, exposed service conduits overhead, plain partition walls, mirrored column reflecting the poster titled "Formen der Abweichung." A stack of returned art catalogs on a low display shows a folded ISBN (black-and-white barcode) peeking over the edge and tucked under a cheap metal price-rail clip. The Garten-Golum poster's botanical face floats on the partition with softly glowing eyes; a thin paper tendril from the poster is threaded beneath the ISBN sticker. Practical fluorescent fixtures pulse gently; one tube hangs askew,
rawScenePlan.videoPrompt: Start from the still: pulsed fluorescent light and mirrored reflection align the barcode stripes with the poster's plant-face. The poster's eyes blink; the paper tendril slides fully beneath the ISBN sticker and nudges the metal clip — the ISBN sticker peels up and begins to slide forward. The rail releases with a metallic snap; hanging price tags fan outward, one slapping a nearby fluorescent tube so it fractures
rawScenePlan.cameraCue: hesitant reframe with organic micro-sway, then a slight searching pan following the sliding ISBN sticker and the fanning
rawScenePlan.startFrameReason: Begin anchored to the Kaufhaus layout and poster reflection so the precise object placements (folded ISBN sticker under the clip, mirrored column, cracked tube, tendril position)
